capabilityGaps.js: The plugin's firmwareRegression and blend are internal and not exposed as an endpoint; gbsAdjust always appends its own sample, so the doc's pure four-point arithmetic cannot be called through the public surface.

vectors.comment: Direct documentation anchor. The doc's four points are a set, not a stateful V2 step: the appended sample would have to be (50,36) if the current setpoint were 50 um, so encoding this as a gbsAdjust call would silently test a different dataset. The inversion is x = mean_x - mean(y-target)/slope; slope -0.4 clamps to -0.5; 42.5 - 5.0/-0.5 = 52.5; 0.1*50 + 0.9*52.5 = 52.25; lround(522.5) = 523.

vectors.comment: Each call appends (setpoint/10, actual/1000) before predicting. Call 1 appends (35,36) to the three restored points, reproducing the doc's four-point geometry: slope -0.4 clamps to -0.5, prediction 52.5, current 35, blend 0.1*35+0.9*52.5 = 50.75 um -> 508. Call 2 appends (30,38): the five-point slope is also -0.4 and clamps to -0.5, prediction 52.0, blend 0.1*30+0.9*52.0 = 49.8 -> 498. Both calls are outside a zero tolerance and commit.

vectors.source: docs/GBS_PARITY_REVIEW.md:GBS-P06 and tools/gbs_model.py:GbsV2State host replay state (points + lastResultDum); the native GbS2 JSON schema does not carry lastResultDum. Node restores only `points`, not `lastResultDum`.
vectors.comment: Host-replay restart fixture (not the native JSON serializer): restored history (50,30) and restored last result 888. Call 1 appends (50,28); the two-point history has zero variance, so the fallback slope -2.0 gives 50 - 1/-2 = 50.5 um, blend 0.1*50 + 0.9*50.5 = 50.45 -> 505, and |0| < 1000 holds the restored 888. Call 2 appends (40,36): slope -0.7, prediction 51.4286 um, blend 0.1*40 + 0.9*51.4286 = 50.2857 -> 503. A host that drops lastResultDum would return 500 in call 1; that gap is recorded in capabilityGaps and GBS-P06.

capabilityGaps.js: The shipped plugin restores only body.points; the restored last result 888 in call 1 is not reachable through the public surface, so the hold value would be 500. The cross-language part of this fixture (call 2) is covered by v2/appended-sample-trace.

vectors.source: docs/GBS_ALGORITHMS.md:149-151 (variance threshold 0.001, fallback slope -2.0) and docs/GBS_PARITY_REVIEW.md:GBS-P10.
vectors.comment: Both calls append the same x coordinate (40 um), so variance is exactly 0 <= 0.001 for the two-point call and the fallback slope -2.0 applies in both. Call 1: mean delta 2 s -> 40 - 2/-2 = 41 um; blend 0.1*40+0.9*41 = 40.9 -> 409. Call 2: mean delta -0.5 s -> 39.75 um; blend 39.775 -> 398. A host that computed a real slope from identical x values would divide by zero.

vectors.source: src/recovered/gbs_algorithms.cpp (Dum is a signed int32) and tools/gbs_model.py output_tenths, which uses C round for negatives. Synthetic guard case; negative setpoints are outside the grinder's physical range.
vectors.comment: The single history point is (-1,1); with target 28 s the fallback slope gives -1 - (-27)/-2 = -14.5 um. Blend 0.1*(-1)+0.9*(-14.5) = -13.15 um -> -131.5 -> C round away from zero -> -132. Both operands are negative, so this is the same-sign clamp branch; it proves signed DD values survive the integer ABI and the C rounding rule.
